episodes.title: Introduction to Native American History
episodes.description: Explore the aims and approach of the Native American History series.

episodes.title: Tribal Sovereignty Explained
episodes.description: Explore tribal nations’ inherent sovereignty and the limits placed on their ability to govern themselves.

episodes.title: Myths & Misconceptions About Native Americans
episodes.description: Examine myths and stereotypes about Native Americans, including representations of Thanksgiving, tribal casinos, and government assistance.

episodes.title: What Makes Someone Native American?
episodes.description: We dive into the ways people define and reclaim tribal identity, from blood quantums and federal recognition to language and more.

episodes.title: Why Land Matters to Native Americans
episodes.description: We’ll explore how Native peoples’ long, deep history on their homelands informs their culture, languages, and identity to this day.

episodes.title: What Unites Native Worldviews?
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Native American History, we’ll explore similarities in Native worldviews, from harvest traditions to whoopee cushion jokes.

episodes.title: The Real Impacts of Archaeology on Native Americans
episodes.description: Archaeology and anthropology are amazingly interesting fields, but they also have a legacy of dehumanizing and mistreating Native peoples.

episodes.title: Introduction to Indigenous Knowledge
episodes.description: The scientific method isn’t the only way to gain knowledge—Native people have been learning and innovating in their own ways for millennia.

episodes.title: What are the Fish Wars and Why Do They Matter?
episodes.description: Explore food sovereignty, the effects of colonization on traditional foods, and Native communities' efforts to retain or restore them.

episodes.title: The Truth About Columbus’s “First Contact”
episodes.description: We’ll unpack misconceptions around first contact between Europeans and Natives and explore how Native peoples are still resisting colonialism today.

episodes.title: From the Trail of Tears to Wounded Knee
episodes.description: We’ll unpack the history of the Treaty Era and the Reservation Era, and all the broken promises and ripple effects that came with them.

episodes.title: The History of America’s Indian Boarding Schools
episodes.description: Explore assimilation and allotment policies that sought to erase Native cultures, ways of life, and claims to land.

episodes.title: The Indian Reorganization Act Explained
episodes.description: Explore the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934 and its lasting, contested legacy for Native communities.

episodes.title: The Termination Act & The Tribe That Fought Back
episodes.description: Explore how termination and relocation policies reduced federal recognition of Native nations and encouraged Native people to move to cities.

episodes.title: The Native Takeover of Alcatraz
episodes.description: Explore the activism behind major changes in federal Indian policy and its continuing significance for Native nations.

episodes.title: Introduction to Federal Indian Law
episodes.description: Learn how contemporary federal Indian law affects individuals, tribal nations, and their communities.

episodes.title: The Era of Native Urban Relocation
episodes.description: We’ll learn about the unique challenges for Natives in urban areas—and their important contributions to their communities.

episodes.title: Alaska Natives and Native Hawaiians
episodes.description: We’ll learn how Alaska Natives’ and Native Hawaiians’ history with the U.S. has taken its own distinct course.

episodes.title: A History of Indigenous Women with Lily Gladstone
episodes.description: Explore Native women's roles as war heroes, peacemakers, matriarchs, and activists.

episodes.title: Modern Tribal Governments Explained
episodes.description: Examine how tribal governments maintain sovereignty and distinctive institutions while adapting to contemporary life.

episodes.title: Native Languages & The Indian Education Act
episodes.description: We dig into the ways Native languages were destroyed and the resilient ways tribes are bringing them back to life.

episodes.title: The Land Back Movement Explained
episodes.description: We explore what the Land Back movement does, how it works, and what it means for our shared future on this planet.

episodes.title: Hollywood, Pretendians, and Cultural Appropriation
episodes.description: In this episode of Crash Course Native American History, we explore cultural appropriation, from redface to pretendians, and everything in between.

episodes.title: Traditional Ecological Knowledge and Climate Change
episodes.description: Explore traditional ecological knowledge and the continuing relevance of Native communities’ expertise about their homelands.
